citation: Pool, Christopher A. 2007. Olmec Archaeology and Early Mesoamerica. Cambridge World Archaeology. Cambridge; New York: Cambridge University Press. Hardback ISBN 978-0-521-78312-5; paperback ISBN 978-0-521-78882-3; online ISBN 978-1-139-16714-7. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9781139167147.
notes: Cambridge World Archaeology monograph. Cambridge Core book abstract (accessed 2026-10-11): Olmec archaeological culture in tropical lowlands of southern Veracruz and Tabasco, Mexico; emerged some 3500 years ago; flourished over the next 1000 years; first monumental stone art of Mesoamerica; foundations for Maya and other Mesoamerican civilizations laid during early and middle Formative (stated as over 2400 years ago). TOC lists chapters on Olman, beginnings, Middle Formative transformations, Olmecs and Mesoamerica, Late Formative, and legacy. Seed uses only abstract/TOC-visible scope claims; no invented page numbers. Mother-culture vs sister-cultures debate treated in Notes of civ-olmec, not as settled fact.
